title: Assessing Structural Architecture and Cellular Composition of Murine Bone Ex Vivo
author: Lewis, Frost, et al.

steps.title: Open trabecular dataset in CTAn
steps.instruction: Launch CT Analyzer (CTAn) and load one reconstructed tibia image in 8‑bit format; if the tibia was not scanned upright, re‑orient the dataset in Bruker DataViewer, save as BMP(8) and reload.

steps.title: Define trabecular ROI and threshold
steps.instruction: Navigate to the bottom of the growth plate, set the top of selection, set a bottom Z‑position 100 sections (≈1 mm) below the top, manually draw a region of interest (ROI) around trabecular bone excluding outer solid bone, add a second ROI at the stack bottom (software will interpolate), then apply a binary selection using a lower‑limit threshold of ~100 (adjust as needed) and keep this threshold constant for all samples.

steps.title: Run custom processing and export results
steps.instruction: In the Plug‑ins menu open ‘custom processing’ and sequentially apply: Threshold (default levels matching the set threshold), Despeckle 1 (remove white speckles <10 voxels in 3D), Despeckle 2 (remove black speckles <10 voxels), 3D Model (export .ply using Marching Cube 33 algorithm), and 3D Analysis (select Basic and Additional values and specify a save location). Ensure preferences are set to Bone ASBMR and units to µm or mm, press Play, then open the generated .ply in MeshLab and the .txt in Excel (Data → Text to Columns, comma delimited) to obtain TV, BV, BV/TV, Tb.Th, Tb.Sp, Tb.N, Tb.Pf and other metrics.

steps.title: Open cortical dataset in CTAn
steps.instruction: Launch CT Analyzer, load a reconstructed tibia image in 8‑bit format, scroll to the bottom of the growth plate and set a reference with offset –350 µm and height 100 µm to generate a stack 250–350 µm below the growth plate for cortical analysis.

steps.title: Create cortical and whole‑bone ROIs
steps.instruction: Draw an ROI around cortical bone (exclude trabecular bone) and save as “cortical_bone.roi”. Remove it, draw a second ROI encompassing the entire bone in the same region and save as “whole_bone.roi”.

steps.title: Apply threshold and custom processing for cortical bone
steps.instruction: Use binary selection (from dataset) with a lower‑limit threshold of ~100 (same as trabecular), then in ‘custom processing’ apply Threshold (default), Despeckle (remove white speckles <10 voxels), 3D Model (export .ply with Marching Cube 33), and 2D Analysis (append summary results to file, specify save location).

steps.title: Run BATMAN batch analysis
steps.instruction: Open the BATMAN plug‑in, add the reconstructed TIF file (converted to 8‑bit), select the cortical_bone.roi and run, then repeat with whole_bone.roi. After the run, open the .ply in MeshLab and the .txt in Excel to obtain mean total cross‑sectional tissue area (T.Ar), bone area (B.Ar) and cross‑sectional thickness (Cs.Th). Calculate percent cortical area as (B.Ar / T.Ar) × 100.

steps.title: Dehydrate tibias for calcein embedding
steps.instruction: Place each tibia at room temperature in 70 % ethanol for 48 h, then 80 % ethanol (two changes, 48 h each), 90 % ethanol (two changes, 48 h each), and finally 100 % ethanol (three changes, 48 h each).

steps.title: Infiltrate and polymerize tibias in LR White resin
steps.instruction: Surround tibias with LR White medium‑grade resin at 4 °C for 6 days, changing to fresh resin every other day; then orient tibias longitudinally in fresh resin and polymerize for 16 h at 55 °C.

steps.title: Section tibias and mount slides
steps.instruction: Using a microtome, cut 8 µm longitudinal sections at three depths spaced 30 µm apart, transfer sections onto Superfrost Plus slides.

steps.title: Image calcein sections and calculate bone formation parameters
steps.instruction: Capture images with Osteomeasure (Osteometrics) on a fluorescent microscope at 20× magnification, imaging medial and lateral endocortical surfaces plus metaphyseal trabecular bone. Measure 0.3 mm from the growth plate and acquire six fields of view along each surface (total 3.6 mm). Compute mineral apposition rate (MAR) as average distance between the two calcein labels divided by the labeling interval (Ir.L.Th / Ir.L.t.d). Calculate mineralizing surface (MS/BS) using 100 × (dL.Pm + sL.Pm / 2) / B.Pm (where B.Pm = Ec.Pm). Finally, obtain bone formation rate (BFR) as MAR × (MS/BS) / 100.

steps.title: Stain osteoid on sections
steps.instruction: Rehydrate slides, stain with 0.04 % Fast Green in distilled water for 30 min, wash 1 min under running water, counterstain with 0.1 % Sirius Red in picric acid for 30 min–1 h (use PPE and fume hood), wash until clear, then dehydrate sequentially: 70 % ethanol 2 min, 95 % ethanol 2 min (twice), 100 % ethanol 2 min, xylene 5 min, xylene 2 min, air‑dry 2 min and mount with DPX and a coverslip.

steps.title: Image osteoid and quantify with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Acquire bright‑field images on a ZEISS Axioscan Z1 (Zen blue) at 20× (objective 20x/0.8 Plan Apochromat, camera Hitachi HV‑F203 3 CCD, 1600 × 1200 px, 4.4 µm pixel size). In ImageJ/Fiji, create a freehand ROI around trabecular bone, save to ROI manager, then create a second ROI outlining red‑stained osteoid areas, save, measure each ROI (Ctrl + M), and calculate osteoid percentage as (osteoid area / trabecular bone area) × 100. Convert CZI files to TIFF if necessary.

steps.title: Stain osteoblasts on sections
steps.instruction: Prepare 0.2 % ammonia water. Stain rehydrated sections with hematoxylin for 3 min, wash 5 min under tap water, differentiate in 1 % acid alcohol for 30 s, wash 1 min, immerse in 0.2 % ammonia water for 1 min, wash 5 min, rinse quickly in 95 % ethanol (10 dips), counterstain with aqueous eosin for 5 min, then dehydrate as for osteoid (70 % 2 min, 95 % 2 min twice, 100 % 2 min, xylene 5 min, xylene 2 min), air‑dry 2 min and mount with DPX.

steps.title: Image osteoblasts and calculate coverage
steps.instruction: Capture bright‑field images on the ZEISS Axioscan Z1 (same settings as osteoid). In ImageJ, draw a freehand ROI around trabecular bone, save, then draw ROI around areas lined with multiple cuboidal cells, save, measure each ROI (Ctrl + M) and express osteoblast surface as percentage of bone surface (Ob.S / BS). Convert CZI files to TIFF if needed.

steps.title: Prepare TRAP basic incubation medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 9.2 g sodium acetate anhydrous (112.1 mM) and 11.4 g (+) tartaric acid (76 mM) in distilled water, add 46.65 mL glacial acetic acid, adjust volume to 900 mL, then add 5 M NaOH as needed to bring total volume to 1 L (final pH 4.7–5.0). Store at room temperature for up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare TRAP staining solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 mg Napthol AS‑MX in 1 mL 2‑ethoxyethanol (vortex until clear). Add 50 mL of the TRAP basic incubation medium to a 50 mL Falcon tube, add 1 mL of the Napthol AS‑MX mixture, then add 30 mg Fast Red Violet LB salt and vortex until fully dissolved. Warm the solution at 37 °C for 10 min before use.

steps.title: Stain osteoclasts with TRAP
steps.instruction: Place deparaffinized/rehydrated slides in the pre‑warmed TRAP staining solution and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min–2 h, checking every 10 min under a light microscope until red/violet osteoclasts appear (avoid over‑staining). Rinse slides in distilled water, blot excess water with a paper towel, and mount with aqueous mounting medium and a coverslip. For cultured osteoclasts, fix with 10 % PFA for 10 min, wash 3× PBS, then apply the same TRAP staining protocol.

steps.title: Image osteoclasts and quantify
steps.instruction: Capture bright‑field images on the ZEISS Axioscan Z1 (Zen blue) at 20× (same camera settings). In ImageJ, draw a ROI around trabecular bone, measure the area, then use the counting tool to tally TRAP‑positive osteoclasts within the ROI. Express results as osteoclast number per mm² (OC.N / BS). Convert CZI files to TIFF if required and include scale bars for length conversion.
